cefrAlignment: Matches B2 (CEFR CV: can understand standard spoken language at normal speed, with some difficulty from strong accents or very idiomatic speech): short messages and 180–215-word talks in British and American voices, with UK/US vocabulary contrasts.
examFidelity: IELTS Part 1-style messages and TOEIC Part 4-style talks with detail MCQs are realistic, and the accent tips match ielts.org ('British, Australian, New Zealand and North American') and ETS's description of TOEIC accents.
openConcerns: Browser TTS may not produce real weak forms or linking, and only US and UK voices exist (no Australian or New Zealand voice). A specialist should listen to check that the weak-form gap exercise and the dictation really practise weak forms; real recordings would be better.
The lesson has a TOEFL exam tip but no TOEFL exam tag. This is harmless, but you could add 'Listening – Announcement'.
learnerOutcome: A learner can follow British and American voices, recognise floor, time, date and vocabulary differences, and use stressed content words and grammar to recover weak words they miss.
